territorial_scope.description: State statute reaching for-profit entities that conduct business in Rhode Island or produce products or services targeted to state residents, including out-of-state entities.

evidence.quote: produce products or services that are targeted to residents of the state

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Rhode Island act (H 7787 Sub A, adding R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 6-48.1) requiring for-profit controllers of personal data above customer-count thresholds to disclose data practices, honour customer rights and assess heightened-risk processing, enforced by the attorney general as a deceptive trade practice. Takes effect 1 January 2026.
summary.long: Adds R.I. Gen. Laws ch. 6-48.1. Applies to for-profit entities doing business in Rhode Island or targeting residents that, in the preceding calendar year, processed personal data of at least 35,000 customers, or of 10,000 customers while deriving over 20% of gross revenue from data sales. Excludes state bodies, nonprofits, higher-education institutions, GLBA financial institutions, HIPAA covered entities and several other data categories. Controllers must disclose data categories, third parties receiving sold data and a contact mechanism, maintain data security, and obtain consent for sensitive data, including data of known children. Customers may confirm, access, correct, delete, port and opt out of targeted advertising, sales and certain profiling; controllers may not discriminate for exercising rights, and consent revocation takes effect within 15 days. Requests are answered within 45 days, extendable by 45, with 60-day appeals. Processors are bound by contract terms. Data protection assessments are required for targeted advertising, sales, risky profiling and sensitive data processing. The attorney general has sole enforcement authority; violations are deceptive trade practices, and intentional unlawful disclosures carry fines of $100 to $500 per disclosure. No private right of action. Effective 1 January 2026.

notes: The document is the Substitute A bill text (LC005266/SUB A/2, introduced 2024-02-29) and contains no enactment record, so adoption and the session-law citation are not confirmed by this text. Internal inconsistencies: Sec. 1(2) refers to 20% of profit from the sale of personally identifiable data, while Sec. 6-48.1-4(a)(2) and Sec. 6-48.1-5(a)(2) use gross revenue from the sale of personal data. The Explanation says a fine is imposed for each violation, but Sec. 6-48.1-8(a) imposes the $100 to $500 fine only for intentional disclosures described in (a)(1) and (a)(2). Sec. 6-48.1-5(c) and Sec. 6-48.1-7(v) use covered entity, a HIPAA term defined in Sec. 6-48.1-2(9), where other provisions use controller. Sec. 6-48.1-3(d) and Sec. 6-48.1-10(c) carve out nonprofit and tax-exempt bodies in overlapping ways. Effective date is January 1, 2026 (Sec. 3); Sec. 6-48.1-7(i) applies data protection assessments only to processing activities created or generated after January 1, 2026.

"Affiliate" means any entity that shares common branding with another legal entity directly or indirectly, controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with another legal entity.
"Biometric data" means data generated by automatic measurements of an individual's biological characteristics
"Business associate" has the same meaning as provided in 45 C.F.R. § 160.103.
"Child" has the same meaning as provided in 15 U.S.C. § 6501.
"Consent" means a clear, affirmative act signifying a customer has freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous agreement to allow the processing of personal data relating to the customer.
"Controller" means an individual who, or legal entity that, alone or jointly with others determines the purpose and means of processing personal data.
"Covered entity" has the same meaning as provided in 45 C.F.R. § 160.103.
"Customer" means an individual residing in this state acting in an individual or household context.
"Dark pattern" means a user interface designed or manipulated with the substantial effect of subverting or impairing user autonomy, decision-making or choice

definitions.term: Decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects concerning the customer

evidence.quote: "Decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects concerning the customer" means decisions made by the controller that result in the provision or denial by the controller of financial or lending services, housing, insurance
"De-identified data" means data that cannot reasonably be used to infer information about, or otherwise be linked to, an identified or identifiable individual, or a device linked to such individual.
"Identified or identifiable individual" means an individual who can be readily

"Institution of higher education" means any individual who, or school, board, association, limited liability company or corporation that, is licensed or accredited to offer one or more programs of higher learning leading to one or more degrees.
"Nonprofit organization" means any organization that is exempt from taxation under Section 501(c)(3), 501(c)(4), 501(c)(6) or 501(c)(12) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986
"Personal data" means any information that is linked or reasonably linkable to an identified or identifiable individual and does not include de-identified data or publicly available information.
that directly identifies the specific location of an individual with precision and accuracy within a radius of one thousand seven hundred fifty feet (1,750').
"Processor" means an individual who, or legal entity that, processes personal data on behalf of a controller.

"Profiling" means any form of automated processing performed on personal data to evaluate, analyze or predict personal aspects related to an identified or identifiable individual's economic situation, health, personal preferences, interests, reliability, behavior, location or movements.
"Pseudonymous data" means personal data that cannot be attributed to a specific individual without the use of additional information
"Publicly available information" means information that is lawfully made available through federal, state or municipal government records or widely distributed media
"Sale of personal data" means the exchange of personal data for monetary or other

"Sensitive data" means personal data that includes data revealing racial or ethnic origin, religious beliefs, mental or physical health condition or diagnosis, sex life, sexual orientation or citizenship or immigration status

"Targeted advertising" means displaying advertisements to a customer where the advertisement is selected based on personal data obtained or inferred from that customer's activities over time and across nonaffiliated Internet websites or online applications
"Third party" means an individual or legal entity, such as a public authority, agency or body, other than the customer, controller or processor or an affiliate of the processor or of the controller.

obligations.summary: Commercial websites and internet service providers must designate a controller. Where they collect, store and sell personally identifiable information, the controller must identify in its customer agreement or a conspicuous location the categories of personal data collected, the third parties to whom it has sold or may sell such data, and an active contact mechanism.
obligations.conditional_on: Commercial website or internet service provider conducting business in Rhode Island; the identification items apply where it collects, stores and sells personally identifiable information

evidence.quote: then the controller shall, in its customer agreement or incorporated addendum, or in another conspicuous location

obligations.summary: A controller that sells personal data to third parties or processes personal data for targeted advertising must clearly and conspicuously disclose such processing.
obligations.conditional_on: Controller sells personal data to third parties or processes personal data for targeted advertising

evidence.quote: the controller shall clearly and conspicuously disclose such processing.

obligations.summary: The controller must establish, implement and maintain reasonable administrative, technical and physical data security practices to protect the confidentiality, integrity and accessibility of personal data.
obligations.conditional_on: Controller within the scope test: for-profit entity that controlled or processed data of at least 35,000 customers (excluding payment-only processing), or at least 10,000 customers and derived more than 20% of gross revenue from sale of personal data, in the preceding calendar year

evidence.quote: The controller shall establish, implement, and maintain reasonable administrative, technical and physical data security practices

obligations.summary: The controller may not process sensitive data concerning a customer without customer consent, and may not process sensitive data of a known child unless consent is obtained and processing follows COPPA. Controllers complying with COPPA verifiable parental consent are deemed compliant with the parental consent obligation.
obligations.conditional_on: Controller within the scope test in 6-48.1-4(a); processing of sensitive data

evidence.quote: The controller shall not process sensitive data concerning a customer without obtaining customer consent

obligations.summary: The controller may not process personal data in violation of state laws, or in violation of federal laws prohibiting unlawful discrimination against customers.
obligations.conditional_on: Controller within the scope test in 6-48.1-4(a)

evidence.quote: The controller shall not process personal data in violation of the laws of this state

obligations.summary: The controller must provide customers a mechanism to grant and revoke consent to collect, store and sell their personally identifiable information, suspend processing as soon as practicable upon revocation, and effectuate revocation within no longer than fifteen (15) days of receipt.
obligations.conditional_on: Controller within the scope test in 6-48.1-4(a)

evidence.quote: The controller shall provide customers with a mechanism to grant and revoke consent

obligations.summary: Customers have rights to confirm processing and access personal data, correct and delete data, obtain a portable copy where processing is automated, and opt out of targeted advertising, sale of personal data, or profiling in furtherance of solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects. The controller must honour these rights, and customers may exercise them through means the controller establishes and describes in its privacy notice.
obligations.conditional_on: Controller within the scope test in 6-48.1-5(a)

evidence.quote: A customer shall have the right to:

obligations.summary: The controller may not discriminate against a customer for exercising customer rights, and may not deny goods or services, charge different prices or rates, or provide a different level of quality if the customer does not consent to use of their data. A covered entity need not provide a service requiring data collection where the customer opts out. Bona fide loyalty and similar programs are excepted.
obligations.conditional_on: Controller within the scope test in 6-48.1-5(a)

evidence.quote: No controller shall discriminate against a customer for exercising their customer rights.

obligations.summary: The controller must respond to a customer request without undue delay and not later than 45 days after receipt, extendable by 45 additional days with notice within the initial period. If declining, it must inform the customer within 45 days with justification and appeal instructions. Information is provided free once per customer per 12-month period, with a fee or refusal permitted only for manifestly unfounded, excessive or repetitive requests. The controller must notify the customer where it cannot authenticate a request, and must deem deletion compliance for data from third-party sources through the stated retention or opt-out steps. Opt-out requests from authorized agents must be honoured where identity and authority are verified.
obligations.conditional_on: Controller within the scope test in 6-48.1-6(a)

evidence.quote: A controller shall respond to the customer without undue delay, but not later than forty-five (45) days after receipt of the request.

obligations.summary: The controller must establish a process for customers to appeal its refusal to act on a request, make the process clearly and conspicuously available, and inform the customer in writing of the action taken or not taken, with reasons, within 60 days after receipt of an appeal. If the appeal is denied, the customer may complain to the attorney general.
obligations.conditional_on: Controller within the scope test in 6-48.1-6(a)

evidence.quote: A controller shall establish a process for a customer to appeal the controller's refusal to take action on a request

obligations.summary: A processor must adhere to the controller's instructions and assist the controller in meeting its obligations. The controller-processor contract must set out processing instructions, nature, purpose, type of data, duration and the rights and obligations of both parties, and require the processor to ensure confidentiality of personnel, delete or return data at the end of services unless retention is required by law, provide information demonstrating compliance, and engage subcontractors only after an opportunity to object under a written contract.
obligations.conditional_on: Processing on behalf of a controller within the scope test in 6-48.1-7(a)

evidence.quote: A processor shall adhere to the instructions of a controller and shall assist the controller

obligations.summary: The processor must allow and cooperate with reasonable assessments by the controller or its designated assessor, or arrange an assessment by a qualified and independent assessor, and provide a report of such assessment to the controller upon request.
obligations.conditional_on: Processing on behalf of a controller within the scope test in 6-48.1-7(a)

evidence.quote: Allow, and cooperate with, reasonable assessments by the controller or the controller's designated assessor

obligations.summary: The controller must conduct and document a data protection assessment for each processing activity presenting a heightened risk of harm to a customer, including targeted advertising, sale of personal data, certain profiling, and processing of sensitive data. A single assessment may cover comparable processing, and an assessment prepared for another law may satisfy this requirement if reasonably similar in scope and effect.
obligations.applies_from: processing activities created or generated after January 1, 2026
obligations.conditional_on: Controller within the scope test in 6-48.1-7(a); processing presents a heightened risk of harm to a customer

evidence.quote: A controller shall conduct and document a data protection assessment for each of the controller's processing activities that presents a heightened risk of harm to a customer.

obligations.summary: The controller must disclose any data protection assessment relevant to an attorney general investigation when the attorney general requires it, and make the assessment available. Assessments are confidential and exempt from public records disclosure, and disclosure to the attorney general does not waive privilege.
obligations.conditional_on: Attorney general requires disclosure in relation to an investigation

evidence.quote: The attorney general may require a controller to disclose any data protection assessment

obligations.summary: Personal data processed under this section must be reasonably necessary and proportionate to the stated purposes, and adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary for those purposes, considering the nature and purpose of collection, use or retention. Such data must be subject to reasonable administrative, technical and physical measures to protect confidentiality, integrity and accessibility.

evidence.quote: Personal data processed by a controller pursuant to this section may be processed to the extent that such processing is reasonably necessary and proportionate

obligations.summary: A controller in possession of de-identified data must take reasonable measures to ensure the data cannot be associated with an individual, publicly commit to maintaining and using it without attempting re-identification, and contractually obligate recipients to comply with the chapter. A controller disclosing pseudonymous or de-identified data must exercise reasonable oversight of contractual commitments and address breaches.
obligations.conditional_on: Controller in possession of de-identified data, or disclosing pseudonymous or de-identified data
